rlds-integrity.surface: leaderboard RLDS lane only; not executed by LeRobot MCP checks

causes.title: Stored normalization stats disagree with the data
causes.explanation: A pipeline that normalizes from the dataset's stored stats trains and infers with these numbers. When they drift from the data, the policy trains on wrong-scaled inputs and fails with a clean loss curve - the openpi #906 pattern, the top community diagnosis for 'low loss, failed robot' on {policy}.
causes.next_step: Recompute meta/stats.json from the data (LeRobot aggregation, or openpi's compute_norm_stats.py for openpi training) and retrain; if the stats came from a converter, fix the converter.

causes.title: The policy normalizes with q01/q99 but the stats have none
causes.explanation: {policy} normalizes with q01/q99 quantiles. If your training pipeline normalizes from the dataset's stats, missing quantiles mean the run either fails on the missing keys or normalizes with quantiles computed elsewhere, by different code - inputs land in a different range than training assumed. Pipelines that compute their own norm stats at train time do not read these, and for them this finding does not explain the failure.
causes.next_step: Check where your training pipeline gets its norm stats. If from the dataset, recompute meta/stats.json with q01/q99 and retrain; if it computes its own at train time, this finding does not apply - look at the other causes.

causes.title: No normalization stats at all
causes.explanation: There are no stats to normalize {policy}'s inputs or outputs with. Training may still run (some pipelines compute their own), but inference without the same stats produces garbage actions.
causes.next_step: Generate meta/stats.json for the dataset and make sure the training run and the deployment load the same stats.

causes.title: Constant or near-constant dims break normalization
causes.explanation: A zero-variance dim divides by ~0 during normalization (Inf/NaN batches) or amplifies sensor noise into a full-scale signal the policy wastes capacity fitting.
causes.next_step: Drop constant dims from the features (and the policy's input dims), or fix the recording so those dims carry signal; then recompute stats.

causes.title: NaN or Inf values in the data
causes.explanation: NaN/Inf frames poison the batch statistics and the loss; training can appear to converge on the surviving batches while the policy learns corrupted input statistics.
causes.next_step: Find the source in recording or conversion, drop the affected episodes (or repair the frames), recompute stats, and retrain.

causes.title: Episodes shorter than the policy's action chunk
causes.explanation: {policy} predicts action chunks; episodes shorter than the chunk train on padded or truncated actions, teaching the policy boundary artifacts instead of task behavior.
causes.next_step: Drop or merge the short episodes, or train with a smaller action horizon (pass it back as a policy override here to re-check).

causes.title: info.json shapes disagree with the data
causes.explanation: The declared feature shapes are what the policy builds its input/output layers from; a mismatch means the policy sees a different layout than the metadata promises - training against the metadata fails or silently truncates dims.
causes.next_step: Fix meta/info.json to the actual array shapes (or fix the conversion that wrote it) before training.

causes.title: Long idle segments teach the policy to do nothing
causes.explanation: Episodes with long stretches where no joint moves teach {policy} that doing nothing is a good action - the classic 'robot stays still at inference' postmortem. Idle at the end of episodes is worse: it teaches stopping early.
causes.next_step: Trim the idle segments (or the worst episodes) and retrain; if the idling is an artifact of how demonstrations start/end, fix the recording flow.

causes.title: A joint barely moves - or never moves
causes.explanation: A joint that never moves teaches {policy} to ignore that degree of freedom; a gripper that never actuates in pick/place episodes means the demonstrations never show the grasp the task needs.
causes.next_step: Check whether the joint/gripper is an unused DOF (fine - consider dropping the dim) or a recording/hardware failure (re-record); a commanded joint whose follower never moves points at a dead or blocked motor.

causes.title: v3 episode metadata points at the wrong parquet shard (converter rollover bug)
causes.explanation: The v2.1-to-v3.0 converter wrote the file-rollover boundary episode into the new shard but left its meta/episodes pointer aimed at the previous one (huggingface/lerobot#2401). LeRobot loads only the metadata-named file, so those episodes silently vanish from training while the dataset looks complete on disk - the run just sees less data.
causes.next_step: Re-convert from the v2.1 source with a lerobot build that carries the #2401 fix (or re-export the dataset), then re-run kinema check; until then the flagged episodes never reach training.

causes.title: Metadata points at video files the repo does not contain
causes.explanation: The episode metadata records video shards that are not in the repo. The episode rows all load - the dataset looks complete - but {policy} training that decodes video for those episodes fails on the missing file, or trains with the camera dropped for them.
causes.next_step: Re-export or restore the missing video files the check names; until then, exclude the affected episodes (the finding lists them) from any training that reads video.

causes.title: Stored stats are converter float32 accumulation, not data statistics
causes.explanation: The per-episode stats reproduce a naive float32 accumulation bitwise while disagreeing with the data in float64: the converter computed stats in f32 and its rounding error is stored as if it were data statistics. On constant channels this fabricates a nonzero std and DC-offsets the mean, so a pipeline normalizing from these stats feeds {policy} the converter's rounding error. The data itself is fine.
causes.next_step: Recompute the stats from the data in float64 (LeRobot aggregation or the converter's stats step with an f64 accumulator) and retrain; the episodes themselves need no repair.

causes.title: Leader/follower calibration offset
causes.explanation: On still frames the commanded and measured positions of a joint disagree by a constant offset: the leader and follower arms were calibrated differently. {policy} learns to command a target shifted by that offset; any change in calibration between recording and deployment (a recalibrated arm, a different follower) makes it reach the wrong place.
causes.next_step: Recalibrate leader and follower to the same reference and re-record, or correct the offset in the actions (the finding gives it per joint) and retrain; deploy with the same calibration the data was recorded with.

causes.title: Command and measurement drift apart across the range (scale error)
causes.explanation: The gap between command and measurement grows linearly across the joint's range - a gear-ratio or unit error between leader and follower, not a fixed offset. {policy} learns a distorted mapping that is right near one end of the range and wrong at the other.
causes.next_step: Find the unit or gear-ratio mismatch in the recording or conversion (the finding gives the per-range slope), fix the scale in the actions, and retrain.

causes.title: Gripper calibration drift at its free end
causes.explanation: Even at its free end, where nothing blocks it, the gripper's measured position sits off its command: the gripper's calibration differs between leader and follower. Grasps learned from this data close too early or too late.
causes.next_step: Recalibrate the gripper on both arms and re-record, or correct the gripper offset in the actions and retrain.

causes.title: Commands clipped at a joint limit
causes.explanation: A share of commands during motion sit exactly at a joint's limit value - the teleop or converter clipped them. {policy} imitates the clipped trajectory: it learns to push into the limit instead of the motion the operator intended.
causes.next_step: Check the joint limits in the teleop/recording config and the converter; re-record or drop the most-clipped episodes, and retrain.

causes.title: A camera has no video for some episodes
causes.explanation: Some episodes have no video for a declared camera. {policy} training either fails on those episodes or trains them with the camera silently missing, so the vision encoder sees a modality that comes and goes.
causes.next_step: Restore the missing videos, or exclude the episodes the finding lists from any training that reads that camera.

causes.title: Blurry, dark or overexposed camera frames
causes.explanation: A camera's sampled frames are blurry, underexposed or clipped bright in a share of episodes. Low-quality frames measurably hurt training (HF's GIGO study: 20% low-quality data raised training loss ~30%), and a policy trained on them has less visual signal to act on.
causes.next_step: Look at the episodes the finding names; fix focus/exposure and re-record, or drop the worst episodes and retrain.

causes.title: The policy needs camera input this dataset does not have
causes.explanation: {policy} is a vision policy but the dataset declares no image or video features: it cannot be trained as configured, or trains blind.
causes.next_step: Use a state-only policy for this dataset, or add the camera streams to the recording.

causes.title: The policy conditions on language but no episode has a task string
causes.explanation: {policy} conditions on a language instruction, but no episode declares one - training teaches a task-agnostic policy that ignores whatever instruction you give it at inference.
causes.next_step: Add task strings to the episodes (meta/tasks and each episode's tasks) and retrain.

causes.title: Episodes with empty task strings
causes.explanation: A share of episodes carry an empty task string: language-conditioned training learns that '' is a valid instruction for those demonstrations.
causes.next_step: Fill in the task strings for the episodes the finding lists, or exclude them from language-conditioned training.

causes.title: Frames point at task indices the task table does not define
causes.explanation: Frames reference task_index values with no entry in meta/tasks: the instruction for those frames is unrecoverable, and loaders fail or substitute nothing.
causes.next_step: Rebuild meta/tasks from the source recordings (or fix the converter that renumbered tasks) so every task_index resolves.

causes.title: Timestamps off the sampling grid or non-monotonic
causes.explanation: Frames are not evenly spaced at the declared fps, or time runs backwards. delta_timestamps windows and video-frame lookup then sample the wrong frames: {policy} trains on misaligned observation/action windows.
causes.next_step: Fix the timestamps (or the declared fps) in the conversion, or drop the episodes the finding names, and retrain.

causes.title: Exact duplicate episodes
causes.explanation: Episodes with identical action trajectories: they add no diversity, over-weight those demonstrations, and inflate any metric computed across them.
causes.next_step: Drop the duplicates the finding lists (keep one per group) and retrain.

causes.title: Duplicate episodes span the declared train/eval splits

indicates.message_contains: would be measured on training data

causes.explanation: The same (or nearly the same) episodes appear in more than one declared split: evaluation is measured on training data, so a good eval score says nothing about generalization.
causes.next_step: Move the leaked pairs into one split (or drop them) and re-evaluate before trusting the numbers.

causes.title: Episodes share identical stretches of motion
causes.explanation: Pairs of episodes share identical multi-frame stretches of motion - a splice, a botched merge, or a scripted generator replaying a primitive. Those segments add no diversity and over-weight one motion.
causes.next_step: Inspect the pairs the finding lists; drop or re-record copied segments, or accept them knowingly for scripted data.

causes.title: A handful of episodes are outliers on duration, end pose or jerk
causes.explanation: A few episodes sit far outside the rest on harmful axes (very long/short, a different end pose, jerky motion). Outliers dominate the gradient out of proportion to their count, and are often failed or mislabeled demonstrations.
causes.next_step: Review the episodes the finding lists; drop the broken ones and retrain.

causes.title: Episode metadata disagrees with the data

indicates.message_contains: episode metadata disagrees with the data

causes.explanation: The catalogued length of an episode does not match the rows in the data: loaders that trust the metadata read past the episode, short-change it, or fail outright.
causes.next_step: Rebuild the episode metadata from the data (or re-convert), then re-run kinema check.

causes.title: Data files that cannot be read
causes.explanation: Some data files are corrupt or cannot be fetched: loading the dataset crashes, or those episodes are silently skipped by tools that catch the error.
causes.next_step: Re-upload or regenerate the files the finding names; until then, the dataset cannot be trained on as a whole.

causes.title: Reward carries no signal
causes.explanation: The reward is the same on every frame: RL or reward-conditioned training gets no learning signal from it.
causes.next_step: Recompute the reward in the conversion (or drop the field if you train by imitation only).

causes.title: Episodes never terminate
causes.explanation: done is never True on any frame: RL training never sees an episode end, so value targets bootstrap forever.
causes.next_step: Set done on each episode's last frame in the conversion and retrain.

blind_spots: Unit conventions (degrees vs radians): stats computed on the same data always agree, so self-consistent wrong units are invisible to every check.
Joint-order mismatches between the dataset's layout and the policy's expected layout.
Absolute-vs-delta action space mismatches that only appear at inference (calibration-drift classifies those dims and sits them out by design).
Train-fps vs the deployment control-loop frequency (timestamp-grid checks internal consistency only).
Training pipelines that recompute normalization stats at train time with different code than LeRobot's aggregation (e.g. an openpi run over stats the dataset never ships).
